notes: Utah has no deduction from income. Tax is one flat rate (4.5%) on Utah taxable income (TC-40 line 9, which starts from federal AGI; lines 4 to 9). The federal standard or itemized deduction and the Utah personal exemption do not reduce line 9: they feed the taxpayer tax credit (lines 11 to 20), 6% of (2,111 per dependent + federal standard or itemized deduction - state income tax itemized), less 1.3% of Utah taxable income over a base amount, not below zero. The base.deductions entries record the amounts the booklet prints; they are credit inputs, never income deductions. See relief utah_taxpayer_tax_credit.

credit_basis is left out of utah_taxpayer_tax_credit: 0.06 is a share of line 15 (exemptions plus deductions), which is neither the covered income nor the tax, and the schema has no value for it. cap is left out too: the booklet prints no cap, and line 12 is whatever the federal return shows.

The booklet prints no Utah standard deduction of its own. Line 12: 'Enter your federal standard or itemized deduction from line 12e of your federal return' (PDF page 10). The only printed figures are in the Qualified Exempt Taxpayer Worksheet (PDF page 11, line 2: 15,750 single; 23,625 head of household; 31,500 married filing joint; 15,750 married filing separate, or 0 if the spouse itemized; 31,500 qualifying surviving spouse). They are recorded as the federal amounts the booklet prints. The federal age 65 and blindness extras are excluded for the line 21 test only; line 12 takes federal line 12e, and the sources print no amount for those extras.

Personal exemption: 'The Utah personal exemption is $2,111 per dependent' (PDF page 10, Line 11). Line 2 counts dependents allowed a credit under IRC section 24, and 'You may not claim yourself or your spouse as other dependents' (PDF page 9). A dependent born in 2025 is counted twice (lines 2a and 2c). No age 65 or blindness amount is printed.

Line 14 reduces the credit base by state and local income tax itemized on federal Schedule A (line 5e less 5b and 5c, not below zero; blank for a standard deduction); no field holds it, so it is in the relief's other_conditions.

Brackets: one flat rate of 4.5% from 0 for every status; the booklet prints no separate schedule for married filing separately or head of household. PDF page 4: HB 106 lowered the rate 'from 4.55 percent to 4.5 percent'. Second document: TC-40 line 10, 'multiply line 9 by 4.5% (.045)'.

Another state's government pension, New York State included: not found in the booklet. No entry covers public_pension_other_state and no sentence names one. The subtractions are a closed list of nine codes (PDF page 10, Line 8; PDF page 19; TC-40A web page) and none is a government pension. The nearest sentence: 'Utah residents who earn income in other states must pay Utah tax on that income' (PDF page 7). Such a pension stays in federal AGI on line 4 and is taxed like any other income; only the age-based retirement credit (18), which is not tied to an income kind, or code 90 in its rare case, could apply. That it is taxed is a reading from the closed list, not a printed sentence. No reciprocity rule by paying state is printed.

Utah's own and federal civilian government pensions: not found in the booklet as a separate rule. No subtraction exists for them. PDF page 23 (AJ): military retirement pay 'does not include Social Security income, 401(k) or IRA distributions, or other sources of income, such as non-military federal retirement'. Military retirement pay has its own credit (AJ) and railroad retirement a subtraction (78).

Private pensions, IRA and 401(k) distributions: no subtraction in the booklet; they stay in federal AGI, and only the retirement credit (18) can offset them. Code 90 is limited to qualified section 401(a) plans in 'very rare cases' (PDF page 20). Roth conversions are not mentioned anywhere in the sources; no relief exists to cover them, so covers_unclear is not needed.

Social Security: no subtraction line and no sentence that benefits are taxed or exempt; none of the nine subtraction codes is Social Security (PDF page 19; TC-40A web page). The Utah base is federal AGI, so taxable benefits stay in line 9, and a credit gives relief: AH, 4.5% of taxable benefits (federal 1040 line 6b, less any amount in codes 77 or 78), 'You may only claim this credit for Social Security benefits included in adjusted gross income on this return' (PDF page 23), less 2.5% of modified income over the threshold. Treatment 'relief'.

Retirement credit (18), Social Security Benefits Credit (AH), Military Retirement Credit (AJ): 18 cannot go with AH or AJ, for either spouse on a joint return: 'You may not claim this credit if you (or your spouse, if filing jointly) claim either the Social Security Benefits Credit (code AH) or the Military Retirement Credit (code AJ)' (PDF page 21), and AH and AJ each repeat it for code 18 (PDF page 23). AH and AJ can combine: each names only code 18 as its bar, and nothing printed bars one with the other, so neither lists the other in cannot_combine_with. No best_of_group is used, because that would make AH and AJ alternatives; the filer chooses 18, or AH and/or AJ.

Retirement credit worksheet: 450 per qualifying person (900 when both spouses take it, line 1), and one reduction (2.5% of modified AGI over the threshold) taken from that total (line 10). 'the maximum amount of this credit is $450 per individual' (PDF page 21). The credit is tied to no kind of income: covers is all_income because the text says only 'born on or before Dec. 31, 1952'.

Measures: the retirement credit's modified AGI starts from TC-40 line 6 and the Social Security credit's from line 9; each subtracts the code 57 municipal addition and adds all federal tax-exempt interest (1040 line 2a). So interest added at code 57 is not counted twice. base is 'other' because no schema base subtracts code 57; the definition is in as_printed. The taxpayer tax credit's measure is line 9 itself.

Qualified Exempt Taxpayer (line 21): the whole Utah tax is zero when federal AGI is at or below the federal standard deduction (without age or blindness extras) plus the federal enhanced deduction for seniors (federal Schedule 1-A line 37). PDF page 4 says 'less than' while Line 21 says 'less than or equal' and the worksheet says line 5 is zero; the worksheet governs. The senior amount is not a fixed number and the sources print none, so the threshold is the standard deduction only and the senior add-on is in as_printed. The income test keeps the relief at the threshold itself and removes it above.

Municipal interest: Utah bonds exempt (subtraction 71 only when the interest is in federal AGI, such as Build America Bonds). Non-Utah bonds acquired after Jan. 1, 2003 are added back (code 57) unless 'the issuer does not impose an income tax on bonds issued by Utah, or the issuing state does not impose an income tax' (PDF page 18). Because the add-back depends on the issuing state's rule, treatment is 'other'.

Capital gains: the booklet prints no separate rate or deduction for gains, so capital_gains is empty; not found in the booklet that gains are taxed like ordinary income, though the flat rate and base imply it. Two credits tie to gains (04, 26), both recorded as reliefs.

All the credits recorded are nonrefundable: 'You may not carry forward or back any credit that is more than your tax liability' (AH, AJ, 04, 26, AA) and 'any retirement credit' (18). Line 24: they 'can reduce your income tax to zero, but cannot result in a refund' (PDF page 11). The schema holds no field for that.

Not recorded as reliefs: Native American income (77; the Social Security worksheet takes benefits in it out), equitable adjustments (69, 79), FDIC premiums (89), trust items, MSA and my529 addbacks, the state tax refund on line 7, the lump sum distribution addition (51, 'only applies if you filed form 4972'), the credit for income tax paid to another state (17, PDF page 26), and credits unrelated to retirement income (child tax credit, earned income credit, adoption, childcare and others). Line 51 is the only retirement-income addition.
Indexing: the sources say nothing about inflation adjustment of the rate, the 2,111 exemption, the base phase-out amounts or the credit thresholds. Recorded as not_stated.
No surtax and no recapture of lower brackets is printed; the 1.3% credit phase-out is a relief income test, not a recapture.
